q: For the first 9 days, we had improvement every night, started with 40 minutes of crying or fussing before sleep, to eventually around 5 minutes after a week. to then 2 night of no tears at bedtime.
cx: Adjusted Ferber with shorter check-ins for a 6-month-old.

q: Overwhelmed by what to do next, and afraid not addressing naps + teething is going to sabotage sleep training.
cx: A tooth arrived on day 10, just after dropping to two naps.

q: It’s currently 4am where I am. My 5 week old has been up since 1am and has just been crying. This is what it has looked like for the past 5 weeks.
cx: Parent of a 5-week-old and a 2-year-old; husband back at work.

q: People keep saying “it’ll get better, by three months she’ll turn a leaf” and that only pisses me off more because that’s 9 weeks away.. how am I meant to do this
cx: The 'three months' reassurance lands badly.

q: He looks after my two year old at night because she wakes everytime the baby cries which is a lot. He is probably getting a tiny bit more sleep than me which isn’t a lot.
cx: How the couple divide two children's nights.

q: Also, I’m scared of creating a water association that will make her wake more often. Am I crazy?
cx: Parent of a 17-month-old who wakes 2-3 times a night, sometimes 90 minutes to resettle.

q: I don’t want to let her cry it out. We’ve tried letting her settle by herself at night when she doesn’t even wanna be touched and it didn’t work. She only cried louder lol.
cx: Planning a move to her own room without crying methods.

q: I’m SORRY I gave so many details but in my mind they’re all relevant
cx: Apologises for the length of her post.

q: I feel betrayed by everyone who has ever said that cosleeping got them more sleep!
cx: Mother of three; first child she has coslept with, at 11 months.

q: We’ve tried the gentle methods that worked for our girls, but this guy does not relent.
cx: Methods that worked for older siblings fail on the third.

q: I don’t agree that teaching your kids to sleep on their own by making them cry it out is a part of parenting. I prefer to support my children to sleep.
cx: Pushes back on commenters recommending crying methods.

q: For now I’m just yelling into the void and maybe there are other parents out there who can relate or at least tell me that their kid did start sleeping better all by themself
cx: Wants company, not a method.

q: I follow wake windows of 50-1.75 min, but this means she needs like 6-7 naps a day if it’s 10 min naps!
cx: 10-week-old who only naps long on the go; the parent's first baby was also a short napper.

q:
We’re currently bouncing and rocking her to sleep and this can easily take over an hour, but our backs can’t do it for much longer. 

We’ve tried Ferber method twice for 5 nights at both 8 and 9 months, but I gave in after about 1.5hrs. She was standing and crying the whole time and didn’t lie down once.
cx: 10-month-old sleeps through but has never fallen asleep independently.

q: I need to hear some CIO success stories for independent sleep.
cx: Opening line, the night before starting CIO.

q: I wish I had sleep trained for independent sleep and not just night wakings before she could stand 😂 lesson learned
cx: Same parent.

q: Well I’ll be damned. It took her 15 mins to fall asleep last night and then 9 mins for her nap this morning. I’m speechless!
cx: Update two days later.

q: The dummy used to work really well for resettling, but now it often doesn't. We're increasingly having to pick her up, and sometimes she needs 10–30 minutes of breastfeeding/comfort before she'll sleep again.
cx: 5-month-old waking every 10-80 minutes after a better spell; long list of things tried.

q: We're not looking to do full CIO/extinction right now. We're open to gentle sleep training and making changes to her schedule/settling, but we're struggling to work out what the actual problem is.
cx: Same mother.

q: Its so exhausting! No one warned me about this part 😂 I hope things start to get better for us all soon! We have a holiday in September that I am dreading now in case her sleep is still like this!
cx: A planned holiday becomes a worry.

q: Ever since we moved, he goes to sleep at 7pm, but after around 2 to 3 hours he wakes up fully awake. Not crying, not fussing. Just full on chatting, rolling, eating his feet.
cx: 5.5-month-old after a move from California to Austria, nine hours ahead.

q: The first day we arrived I was so exhausted and then I had to listen to his chatting for 3 hours in the middle of the night. I overslept my alarm and he did too. We both slept until 11am.
